messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the oscillating body. Body velocity relative to the surrounding fluid is the primary kinematic parameter. Parameter values also involve the damping coefficient, which depends on the fluid's viscosity and the pendulum's geometry. Geometry of the pendulum determines how much resistive drag the medium exerts on it. It should be taken into account in the physical pendulum model when oscillations occur in a fluid medium such as air or a liquid. Medium viscosity and the resulting energy dissipation become important when the amplitude decays significantly over successive oscillations. Oscillations then become damped, and the equation of motion must include a velocity-dependent dissipative term.

- The coefficient of viscosity of the fluid (η)
- The velocity of the object relative to the fluid

- The pendulum swings in a fluid (air or liquid)
